$comment: The icon ROLE VOCABULARY — the contract between chartcore (which emits
sentinel colours) and the theme JSON in the Python backend (which gives
each role a hex per palette). Neither side may invent a role name; both
read this file.
WHY SENTINELS AND NOT TOKENS: chartcore normalises every icon through
usvg, which bakes <style>/class down to concrete fill/stroke attributes
and drops the stylesheet — measured, not assumed. So a role cannot ride
as CSS. It rides as a reserved HEX that survives usvg untouched, and the
client string-substitutes it for the palette's real hex immediately
before rasterising. Rendered output is verified to contain ONLY #rrggbb
notation (no rgb(), no named colours except 'none'), so a plain hex
substitution reaches every painted value.
SENTINEL BLOCK: #fe00XX, XX = the role's index below. No real artwork hex
collides with that block (the vendored set uses 18 distinct hexes, listed
in `retired_hexes` per role).
OPT-IN: chartcore emits sentinels only when asked (render_aton_icon's
`roles` flag). Default output stays day-baked and byte-identical, so the
Rust and frontend halves of this migration each land green on their own.
DAY IS THE PROOF: `day` below is exactly what the icon renders today. A
role-substituted day icon must be byte-identical to the baked one. That
is the acceptance test for the whole colour pipeline.

lit-generic.note: lights keep their OWN palette — upstream genicons.py does, and the hexes differ from the object colours of the same name

lit-white.note: shares day hex with lit-yellow — a faithful upstream quirk, NOT a typo. Two roles so a theme MAY separate them; day must not.

ink.note: the .outline/.baseline stroke and .basepoint stroke. Baked in RUST, not in palette.rs and not in any asset — the role MIGRATION.md stage 3 forgot. This is the single most important role for a dark palette: it is the outline of every parametric buoy.

paper.note: .basepoint fill — the disc a buoy body sits on.

art-ink.note: CMYK registration black; the literal icons' equivalent of `ink`

warn-magenta.note: IHO warning magenta. Distinct role from obj-magenta despite the identical day hex: obj-magenta is an S-57 COLOUR value on a buoy, this is chart furniture (TSS arrows, restricted-area hatch). A paper theme wants them different.

art-stroke.note: REAL production paint — measured on 98 keys (TOPSHP/7/*), not editor cruft as first assumed. It is an inline style="stroke:#333333" on UNCLASSED paths: the X/cross strokes are the artwork itself but sit outside the .outline/.fill role system, so an x-shape topmark renders grey no matter which S-57 COLOUR is requested. Giving it a role makes it follow the theme; making it follow the REQUESTED COLOUR needs the asset reclassed, which is a separate fix (it would change rendered bytes for those 98 keys).

$comment: MEASURED AFTER THE FACT: only 24 of the 35 roles above are ever emitted.
The 11 below reach nothing. They are kept (not deleted) so the indices
stay stable against the sentinel table already baked into roles.rs, and
so the mistake stays visible. Theme JSON authored for them is inert.
The four art-grey-* roles are an error in this very file: they came from
a SOURCE-side grep and are `inkscape:deskcolor` / `bordercolor` editor
metadata, not paint. That is precisely the failure the $measurement block
below warns about — written before the roles were, and not applied to
them. 21 rendered hexes needed 21 roles, not 35; the arithmetic was
there to be checked and was not.
The seven dead lit-* roles are a different thing and NOT an error here —
they are unreachable because of a bug in chartcore, described below.
lit_roles_are_unreachable: recolor_variant resolves a colour word as colour_hex(name).or_else(light_colour_hex(name))
— object table FIRST. Every LIGHT_COLOURS word except `generic` also exists in
OBJECT_COLOURS, so the light table is never consulted for them and only lit-generic
That is a REAL upstream-parity bug, not just dead roles: genicons.py gives light/white
#fab20b and light/orange #fa870b, and chartcore renders #ffffff and #f7a837. Lights are
the highest-value dusk/night case, so this is worth its own task. Fixing it changes day
bytes, which is why it was not folded into the sentinel work.

$measurement: The day values above are the RENDERED surface, not the source surface —
they differ. Swept the whole production key space (136 plain literals, 36
parametric x 14 colour words, BOYSHP/BCNSHP/TOPSHP x 40 shapes x 5 colpats
x 7 colour lists): 21 distinct hexes, zero render errors. Every one has a
role. A source-side grep would have missed #333333 as production paint and
invented a role for #ff0000, which renders on no production key at all.
#ff0000 and the bare `grey`/`red` named colours appear ONLY when a
parametric icon is rendered through the 1-segment literal form, which
leaves COLORING{} unsubstituted and lets the vendored file's Inkscape
PREVIEW stylesheet survive. No production key reaches that path. Worth
